knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

Libraries and Packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
SurveyResponses <- read_excel("SurveyResponses.xlsx")
View(SurveyResponses)

#Summary of all variables
summary(SurveyResponses)

#Frequency tables
table(SurveyResponses$Gender)
table(SurveyResponses$`Age Group`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Health Insurance`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Healthcare Checkup`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Sexual Behaviors`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Positive STI Test`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Housing Situation`)
table(SurveyResponses$Cost)

#Cross tabs
table(SurveyResponses$Gender, SurveyResponses$`Healthcare Checkup`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Health Insurance`, SurveyResponses$`Healthcare Checkup`)
table(SurveyResponses$Gender, SurveyResponses$`Health Insurance`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Sexual Behaviors`, SurveyResponses$`Positive STI Test`)
table(SurveyResponses$Gender, SurveyResponses$`WillingnessTest`)
table(SurveyResponses$`Sexual orientation`, SurveyResponses$`WillingnessTest`)
table(SurveyResponses$Gender, SurveyResponses$`WillingnessTestPaid`)

#Chi square tests
tbl_gender_willingnesstest <- table(SurveyResponses$Gender,SurveyResponses$`WillingnessTest`)
chisq.test(tbl_gender_willingnesstest, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
fisher.test(tbl_gender_willingnesstest)

tbl_behavior_sti <- table(SurveyResponses$`Sexual Behaviors`,SurveyResponses$`Positive STI Test`)
chisq.test(tbl_behavior_sti, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
fisher.test(tbl_behavior_sti)

tbl_behavior_willingnesstest <- table(SurveyResponses$`Sexual Behaviors`,SurveyResponses$`WillingnessTest`)
chisq.test(tbl_behavior_willingnesstest, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
fisher.test(tbl_behavior_willingnesstest)

tbl_behavior_willingnesstestpaid <- table(SurveyResponses$`Sexual Behaviors`,SurveyResponses$`WillingnessTestPaid`)
chisq.test(tbl_behavior_willingnesstestpaid, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
fisher.test(tbl_behavior_willingnesstestpaid)

#Logistic regression
SurveyResponses <- SurveyResponses %>%
  mutate(
    willingness_test_binary = case_when(
      `WillingnessTest` %in% c("Definitely Willing", "Probably Willing") ~ 1,
      `WillingnessTest` %in% c("Unsure", "Probably Not Willing", "Definitely Not Willing") ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    `Sexual Behaviors` = as.factor(`Sexual Behaviors`)
  )

SurveyResponses <- SurveyResponses %>%
  mutate(
    willingness_test_paid_binary = case_when(
      `WillingnessTestPaid` %in% c("Definitely Willing", "Probably Willing") ~ 1,
      `WillingnessTestPaid` %in% c("Unsure", "Probably Not Willing", "Definitely Not Willing") ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


#Models
model_logit <- glm(
  willingness_test_binary ~ `Sexual Behaviors`,
  data = SurveyResponses,
  family = binomial
)
summary(model_logit)


model_logit_paid <- glm(
  willingness_test_paid_binary ~ `Sexual Behaviors`,
  data = SurveyResponses,
  family = binomial
)
summary(model_logit_paid)


model_logit_multi <- glm(
  willingness_test_binary ~ `Sexual Behaviors` + Gender + `Health Insurance` + `Age Group`,
  data = SurveyResponses,
  family = binomial
)
summary(model_logit_multi)



#Score drop offs
# WillingnessTest (willing to use a test kit) 
#Definitely willing: 17, Probably willing: 7, Unsure: 5 Probably not willing: 0, Definitely not willing: 0 
# WillingnessTestPaid (willingness to pay for a test kit) Definitely willing: 7, Probably willing: 9, Unsure: 10, Probably not willing: 2, Definitely not willing: 1 

score_map <- c(
  "Definitely Willing" = 5,
  "Probably Willing" = 4,
  "Unsure" = 3,
  "Probably Not Willing" = 2,
  "Definitely Not Willing" = 1
)

willingnesstest_counts <- c(
  "Definitely Willing" = 17,
  "Probably Willing" = 7,
  "Unsure" = 5,
  "Probably Not Willing" = 0,
  "Definitely Not Willing" = 0
)

willingnesstest_counts <- c(
  "Definitely Willing" = 7,
  "Probably Willing" = 9,
  "Unsure" = 10,
  "Probably Not Willing" = 2,
  "Definitely Not Willing" = 1
)

df <- data.frame(
  Category = names(free_counts),
  Free = as.numeric(free_counts),
  Paid = as.numeric(paid_counts)
)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(Change = Paid - Free)

df


# Visuals
unique(SurveyResponses$WillingnessTest)
unique(SurveyResponses$WillingnessTestPaid)

IndividualDropoff <- SurveyResponses %>%
  mutate(
    WillingnessTest_num = score_map[WillingnessTest],
    WillingnessTestPaid_num = score_map[WillingnessTestPaid],
    dropoff = WillingnessTest_num - WillingnessTestPaid_num
  )

table(IndividualDropoff$dropoff)

# Summary
summary_dropoff <- IndividualDropoff %>%
  summarise(
    avg_dropoff = mean(dropoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_dropoff = median(dropoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_dropoff = sd(dropoff, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

summary_dropoff

# Histogram 
hist(IndividualDropoff$dropoff,
     breaks = seq(-4, 4, by = 1),
     main = "Histogram of Individual Score Drop-offs",
     xlab = "Drop-off Amount (Free - Paid)",
     col = "skyblue",
     border = "black")


# Likert scale questions
# SampleCollectionCorrect, AccurateResults, AccuratelyInterpretResults,PositiveTestNextSteps
score_map <- c(
  "strongly agree" = 5,
  "somewhat agree" = 4,
  "neither agree nor disagree" = 3,
  "somewhat disagree" = 2,
  "strongly disagree" = 1
)

SurveyResponses_clean <- SurveyResponses %>%
  mutate(
    SampleCollectionCorrect_num = score_map[str_to_lower(str_trim(SampleCollectionCorrect))],
    AccurateResults_num = score_map[str_to_lower(str_trim(AccurateResults))],
    AccuratelyInterpretResults_num = score_map[str_to_lower(str_trim(AccuratelyInterpretResults))],
    PositiveTestNextSteps_num = score_map[str_to_lower(str_trim(PositiveTestNextSteps))]
  )

# Compute averages for each column
averages <- SurveyResponses_clean %>%
  summarise(
    SampleCollectionCorrect_avg = mean(SampleCollectionCorrect_num, na.rm = TRUE),
    AccurateResults_avg = mean(AccurateResults_num, na.rm = TRUE),
    AccuratelyInterpretResults_avg = mean(AccuratelyInterpretResults_num, na.rm = TRUE),
    PositiveTestNextSteps_avg = mean(PositiveTestNextSteps_num, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

averages

# Identify which column has the highest average
highest_avg <- names(averages)[which.max(averages)]
highest_avg

```
